html: Hi folks.  I have a bit of good news.  The publishing house has agreed to all the things my agency (Janklow & Nesbit) considered show stoppers.  Now we’re only waiting on the revised contract.  As soon as we get that and I sign it, I’ll let you know.  After that, their editor will want to edit each of the novels.  As soon as I approve the edit, then we should see everything come out under the new imprint.  That includes Wormhole.  Thank you again for your patience.  I’m sure my literary hero, Dean Koontz, could have accomplished all this much more quickly … but probably not before he was … Dean Koontz.

comments.author: Kristian Köhntopp
comments.html:
Hello, I am one of your Amazon Kindle customers, buying through amazon.de (Germany). Will “Wormhole” also be available on Kindle again?

I really liked the first two parts, which I bought on Kindle, and would like to continue reading on that device.

replies.author: Richard Phillips
replies.html: Hi Kristian. Wormhole will definitely be available on the kindle as well as in other ebook formats. I’m hoping that the publisher will release it in eBook formats without waiting for the paperback printing cycle. That’s the plan anyway.

replies.author: Kristian Köhntopp
replies.html: Thanks, that is great news. I am standing by with the mouse pointer hovering over the ‘buy’ button!

comments.author: Dishwater (@Dishwater)
comments.html: I am seeing massive Christmas sales. I think the physical book sales will surprise people.

comments.author: Whit Crowley
comments.html: I was heartened to hear your comment about Kindle availability. I loved your two previous novels which I found because of my love for my Kindle. I have anxiously awaited ‘Wormhole.’ I am glad to hear that you have not forgotten the venue that gave you such a boost.

comments.author: R Brower
comments.html: With the process finally in place, I hope your next books (after Wormhole) will be appearing more quickly. I also hope the Kindle price doesn’t jump exponentially like it seems to with other books once a publisher gets involved.

comments.author: Tom A Freeman
comments.html: Dont get greedy, just sign and publish!
